To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of occult lymph node metastasis (OLNM) is an independent predictor of poor survival in breast cancer patients.
the number of lymph nodes with isolated tumor cells and/or micrometastasis is an independent prognostic factor in breast cancer patients, and that the number of positive lymph nodes is not.

the use of a single, standardized definition for occult lymph node metastasis, isolated tumor cells (ITCs), and micrometasteses in breast cancer patients can improve the comparability of results between different studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new techniques for the study of the structure, properties, and reactions of molecular systems.
the identification and characterization of the genes involved in breast cancer metastasis.
the development of a novel approach to the problem of the detection of breast cancer in patients with breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prognostic significance of occult lymph node metastasis, isolated tumor cells and micrometases is still controversial and that there are many questions that need to be answered.
the prognostic impact of ITCs in breast cancer is controversial and not yet established.
the prognostic significance of occult lymph node metastasis in breast cancer is not well established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of isolated tumor cells (ITCs) or micrometastasis in sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs) is associated with a worse prognosis than the absence of ITCs or micrometases.
it is possible to detect and quantify the expression of a number of proteins, which are involved in the regulation and progression of breast cancer, in a single sample of breast cancer tissue.
the presence of occult lymph node metastasis, isolated tumor cells or micrometastasis is associated with an unfavorable prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of isolated tumor cells (ITCs) or micrometastasis (MM) in sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs) does not have a significant effect on the prognosis of patients with early-stage breast cancer (BC).
the use of a 3D model to screen drugs for efficacy in breast cancer cells is more accurate than using a 2D model.
the use of a combination of the two drugs is more effective than either drug alone, and this effect appears to depend on the presence of both drugs in the same cell at the same time.
